methodology: This experiment started from an empty authoring Git workspace. Authors received the original Graphify capability graph, native symbols and relations. They did not read original production or test bodies, previous rewrites, or original binaries.

The independent verifier ran the pinned original and returned public signatures, configuration/catalog values, model parameter key/shape schemas and input/output observations. Some observations were selected or derived from external validation failures; they were not all independently handcrafted. This supplementary evidence is not encoded in Graphify alone.
External upstream tests and their feedback were used iteratively during implementation and repair. Their final pass rates describe these known checks, not performance on a held-out validation set.

All 89 capability leaves and 367 behavioral details remain in scope. Remaining implementation limitations, failed checks and untested capabilities are visible. This is an experimental reconstruction; full feature equivalence is not established.

Known remaining limitations include canonical DensePose GPS/CSE behavior and unproven exact HRNet/TensorMask equivalence. Mapping every capability to files does not establish implementation completeness or semantic equivalence.

Physical non-test source is measured by the same nanolize-anything inventory for both versions, including native code and scripts. Python in the candidate is consistently formatted before counting. No original runtime is used by the candidate.
Configuration and catalog resources contain declarative data and public constructor references. Their bytes are reported separately; source reduction is not the same as reduction of repository bytes.

The combined byte metric adds measured source bytes and counted runtime JSON/YAML resources. Moving declarative content out of Python can reduce source LOC more than this combined byte total; neither metric measures the size of external datasets, pretrained weights or an installed binary distribution.

Resource bytes include only tracked JSON/YAML under configs, detectron2, projects and densepose, excluding tests, docs, generated output and report bookkeeping. The resource inventory lists every counted file and its hash.

All 66 primary upstream test modules and 15 supporting test/helper/fixture files are byte-checked against the pinned original. CPU and GB200 GPU counts stay separate. Recorded Python/PyTorch/CUDA profiles and per-file pytest import policy must match within each comparison.

Counts use unique node IDs within each environment, with any failed record overriding a pass. Repeated execution records for the same test are not additional cases. Combined node summaries count each environment/test pair once.

Passed / (passed + failed) is the executed-case pass rate. Skips, collection failures, timeouts and baseline-passing cases not completed by the candidate are shown separately. A high executed pass rate can coexist with low coverage.

Per-capability tests are associations derived from imported native symbols, not complete behavioral coverage or precise blame attribution. Detail nodes inherit module metrics and are never claimed independently tested.

Shared source files and test cases can appear under multiple nodes. Group scopes deduplicate their members; only the overall inventory is additive. Preserving graph relationships does not prove integration paths passed.

The project root uses the complete source inventory and matches the overall LOC summary. Candidate files not assigned to a leaf capability remain in the total and are listed as mapping gaps; subgroup counts use only their associated files.

Incomplete processes, collection errors, missing baseline passes and author-declared implementation gaps prevent a green capability status. Synthetic model exercises and COCO subset metrics are separate evidence and never increase immutable upstream test counts.
